_lore:
Oakhollow is a hamlet of a few dozen souls in the forested march of Ashford, in the year of Our Lord 1247.
It belongs to Baron Ulric of Ashford, who has not been seen since Michaelmas; his steward collects the tithe twice a year.
Six weeks ago riders in grey cloaks burned the mill at Fenwick, a day's walk south, and the plague is said to walk with them.
Since then the palisade gate has been barred by the guard Aldric on the steward's order: no one leaves and no one is let in,
though a handful of strangers who arrived before the barring are stuck inside. Food is the worry of every hearth: the barley
harvest was thin, the granary is half empty, and Hilde keeps its key. Three weeks ago the chapel's silver tithe box was stolen
and nobody has confessed; suspicion falls on whoever is disliked that week. The old miller, Edric, died last winter and his
widow Agnes has had no peace since. Marta's tavern, the Crooked Oak, still serves ale, thinner every week. Godric the smith is
forging spearheads instead of ploughshares. Osric the merchant was caught inside with his wares and prices have doubled.
Brother Anselm says Mass at dawn and preaches that the barred gate is a test of faith. Folk here swear by Saint Edmund, distrust
anything from the south, settle small quarrels with fists, and remember every slight until the next feast day.
